evidence_inputs: Plan nova:contour-tree-topology-authority section 2 (v31). Prior review r-20261002T181034474235 scored head e3ee1c90a 55/100 fail with three blocking findings (fd406a1cec1, f74a527259c, f87be44c506). Corrective resume r-20261002T164824351467 attempt-3, write-scoped to tests/test_contour_tree_explanatory_figure.py and benchmarks/contour_tree_explanatory_figure.py, produced head 4c86a9f83. All three blocking findings are resolved and each repair is falsified by a committed negative control. Reviewed manifest baseline_suite and after_suite remain empty. The landing evidence fragment still describes the pre-repair figure and gate and lies outside the corrective round's write scope.

findings.text: In the graph panel the direct labels for the private-region wall maximum and the outside node are placed at the same signed-flux level (both resolve to the wall-contact join level -1.631685e-03 Wb) on adjacent node ranks, each annotated with a fixed (6,6) point offset, so the two label boxes overlap and the word maximum is obscured in the delivered PNG. Per the data-ink rule, when direct labels collide use a frameless legend or stagger the offsets; the caption already carries the multiplicity. This is a residual readability defect the corrective round could have addressed because the benchmark is in that round's scope.

The landing evidence fragment at head still describes the pre-repair figure and guard: line 20 says the poloidal panel overlays nodes 'with the tree's edges dashed between them', and line 25 reports the gate as '2 passed' with the pre-repair DROP_NODE negative control. The delivered figure draws no such edges and the gate now runs 5 tests with three distinct negative controls. The fragment is the plan's reader-facing landing record and now contradicts the artifact it describes. The corrective round's write scope was limited to tests/ and benchmarks/, so the fragment was outside it and this is not a scope failure, but the record must be regenerated by a separately scoped node.

test_committed_figure_files_exist verifies the committed PNG and SVG are present and larger than 1024 bytes but does not compare their content to the receipt, so a stale-but-present render alongside a current receipt would pass. The done-when's reads-the-committed-JSON-SVG-or-PNG requirement is satisfied via the JSON receipt arm; this is a strengthening suggestion, not a gap in the named measure.

justifications.durability: The figure guard now reads a committed artifact: test_committed_receipt_matches_the_computed_tree opens contour-tree-computed.json and compares it to independently rebuilt state, and test_committed_figure_files_exist checks the committed PNG and SVG. A stale receipt fails both (negative control). Gap: the PNG/SVG guard verifies presence and minimum size only, so a stale-but-present PNG alongside a current JSON would pass; and test_figure_draws_exactly_the_receipts_valid_nodes still compares in-memory state rather than an artifact (that path is covered by the committed-file existence test).
justifications.evidence: Three committed negative controls at head falsify each repaired guard (sentinel 1 failed/4 passed EXIT=1; spatial-edges 1 failed/4 passed EXIT=1; stale-receipt 2 failed/3 passed EXIT=1), which proves each guard actually fires rather than merely passing. An independent re-run at reviewed head 4c86a9f83 confirms 5 passed, EXIT=0. Short of full marks because the reviewed run's own positive gate logs still name a prior revision (gate.log 5666c8bcc, 2 passed; repair-gate.log e3ee1c90a, 5 passed) and no single positive head log names 4c86a9f83; the landing evidence fragment also carries a stale gate description.
justifications.fit: Edges are now arcs in the graph panel rather than straight dotted spatial lines, and the sentinel no longer distorts the graph scale, so the figure respects the data-ink rules far better than at e3. Residual: in the graph the direct labels 'wall maximum' and 'outside (wall contact)' occupy the same signed-flux level on adjacent node ranks and overlap, obscuring the word maximum; the data-ink rule says to use a frameless legend or stagger offsets when direct labels collide.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The figure at head 4c86a9f83 renders the computed contour tree honestly: the signed-flux graph axis now spans the physical node levels, the virtual outside sentinel (-1.007 Wb) no longer enters it, and the outside node is drawn and labelled at its wall-contact join level (-1.631685e-03 Wb); the poloidal panel draws no inter-node lines and carries the outside attachment as an explicit diamond at the wall contact. The tree is readable at the real-node scale, so the attachment requirement is met. Residual: two direct labels collide (see finding).
justifications.scope_discipline: The corrective round was granted exactly two paths (tests/test_contour_tree_explanatory_figure.py, benchmarks/contour_tree_explanatory_figure.py). Commit 4c86a9f83 changes those two plus the regenerated figure outputs (PNG, SVG, JSON receipt) and the committed negative-control logs, all within the run's original grant; it adds no unrelated edits.

The attachment is explicit: the poloidal panel draws the outside node as an open diamond at its wall-contact carrier position, and the graph annotates it 'outside (wall contact)'.
